description: Spectral divide-and-conquer via QDWH (QR-based dynamically-weighted Halley) for the polar/sign decomposition, replacing the Newton-Schulz sign iteration that stalls on gapless spectra (its convergence rate collapses for eigenvalues near the split point). Target the big dense gapless shapes 6/7/11 (n=512/1024) currently on the cuSOLVER per-matrix floor. Mechanism: split at the median (rank n/2 by inertia), build the spectral projector via <=6 QDWH iterations of batched CholeskyQR2 + GEMM (tensor-core-friendly, no spectral gap required), project and recurse to small well-separated blocks. Attacks the redundant-work / compute-throughput bottleneck; keep the per-matrix residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback, route guarded per shape.

t1: QDWH sign (QR-form) for shape-11 sign-DC. QDWH gap-independent sign converges (validated 39/39) but the QR-form batched cuSOLVER QR (geqr2_smem_domino_fast) is 82% of shape 11 at n=512 b640 -> 34x regression (shape11 100065->3424775us). QR is what sign-DC exists to avoid; Cholesky inner form is next.

t3: robust QDWH Cholesky (symmetrize Gram + adaptive SPD jitter, l0=1e-8) fixes t2 crash. QDWH 5 iters l_final=1.0 but max||S^2-I||=3.6 > NS ~2e-3: huge early c~5.6e8 amplifies 3xTF32 6e-6 Gram error; shape-11 near-zero eigenvalues 2.4e-7 below precision floor. nbad=67/640 -> shape11 220517us, geomean 30358. QDWH sign doesn't beat NS on this gapless symmetric-about-0 spectrum in 3xTF32.

t4: disable QDWH sign (NS is better), plumbing kept off. Geomean 28540 (parent 28581, no regression). Finding: QDWH-sign precision-limited not gap-limited (FP64 clean 8e-14, FP32 garbage 3.5=NS(18)'s 3.7); NS+membership beats QDWH 0 vs 67/640 fallback on shape 11. Pivoting to the recursion-to-cheap-leaves half of the brief.

t5: depth-2 recursive sign-DC on shape-11 reduced block (QDWH 2nd split). Confirms junk-propagation breaks depth-2: level-1 oversample K=300 -> ~42 junk eigenpairs corrupt level-2 membership -> orth 3.94, nbad=640/640, geomean 31627 (profile: cuSOLVER sytrd = mass fallback). QDWH converges on the reduced block (mean||S^2-I||=0.064) but exact-rank compression between levels is required and unimplemented (variable per-matrix count breaks batching).

t6: consolidate. QDWH sign + depth-2 recursion both plumbed but OFF (measured slower/broken); geomean 28572 = parent 28581 (no regression), 39/39 valid, shapes 6/7/11 at parent (11=99950,7=106695). Profile: reduced-block mega_eigh_med_split_k=42.5% (the recursion target). Full QDWH crossover map documented in code + report.

Explored QDWH spectral D&C for shapes 6/7/11, parent 980c88b geomean 28581us. 6 committed trials; BEST/final = t6 a2379eda geomean 28572 (=parent, no regression, 39/39 valid). QDWH machinery + depth-2 recursion both BUILT and plumbed (flags off).

KEY MEASURED FINDING -- the stall is PRECISION-limited, NOT gap-limited: the brief's premise (QDWH's gap-independence beats NS's ~1/gap stall) does not hold on these benchmark spectra because the eigenvalue nearest the median split sigma is ~1e-7 relative to ||A|| == FP32 epsilon. FP64 QDWH gives clean ||S^2-I||=8e-14 (gap-independence CONFIRMED in exact arith), but FP32/3xTF32 QDWH gives ||S^2-I||=3.5 -- IDENTICAL to NS(18)'s 3.7. FP64 is too slow on B200 (~37 TFLOPS) to exercise QDWH's advantage.

QDWH sign trials on shape 11: t1 QR-form = 34x regression (batched cuSOLVER geqr2 = 82% of shape, exactly what sign-DC avoids). t2/t3 Cholesky-form (robustified: symmetrize Gram + adaptive SPD jitter to survive the huge early c~5.6e8) converges in 4-5 iters but nbad=67/640 (orth 0.0205) vs NS's nbad=0/640 (orth 0.0034) -- NS's benign 1.5X-0.5X^3 gives a smoother near-sigma sign the membership select prefers; QDWH's aggressive dynamic coefficients overshoot near sigma in reduced precision. So NS+K-oversample+membership (the existing path) is strictly better; QDWH adds nothing at the top level here.

RECURSION (brief's 2nd mechanism) crossover map, from direct measurement:
- cuSOLVER super-linear curve CONFIRMED: n=512 b640 dense=170ms, n=256 b640=45ms, n=128 b640=3.9ms; per-matrix n=1024=1766us vs n=512=524us (3.4x). Splitting shape7 1024->2x512 = 40.6ms (120x512) vs 105ms whole = 2.6x headroom.
- shape-11 reduced-block megakernel (K=300, the 42.5%/39ms dominant cost) recursed to K=150 leaves = 14.6ms (3.1x cheaper) -- BUT the 2nd sign-split NS(18) alone costs 25ms, eating the leaf savings.
- t5 depth-2 recursion CONFIRMS the code's prior junk-propagation finding: level-1 oversample (K=300 with ~42 junk cols) corrupts level-2 membership -> orth 3.94, 640/640 fallback. QDWH on the reduced +block DOES converge (mean||S^2-I||=0.064, since the reduced spectrum's near-median eig is ~2e-3 relative == fp32-resolvable), so the blocker is the OVERSAMPLE JUNK, not sign quality.

OPEN DIRECTIONS I did not reach (manager may write briefs):
1. JUNK-FREE recursion via exact-rank compression between levels -- the reduced +block splits cleanly in fp32 (2e-3 gap), so a working depth-2 needs to drop the ~42 junk cols before recursing. The barrier is ragged per-matrix counts (breaks the batched launch); a fixed-width scheme that MASKS junk (not zero-pads, which reintroduces near-zero eigs) could unlock the 3.1x leaf win (~1% geomean on shape 11's 39ms reduced solve). _SIGN_DC_COUNT_SELECT machinery already exists to try count-exact selection.
2. Cheaper 2nd split: the reduced-block spectrum is fp32-resolvable so QDWH(4-6) or NS(6) suffices (vs NS(18)); cutting the 25ms split overhead could tip depth-2 positive IF junk is solved.
3. shape 7 (mixed1024, the ONLY shape purely on cuSOLVER floor, 106ms): 2.6x headroom for a 1024->512 split routing the halves to the EXISTING n=512 fast paths (not the cluster base brief-76 used and regressed). Needs a dense-subset peel + accurate split; the near-median precision wall applies to its dense subset too (measured eig 9e-11 at median on one mixed512 matrix).
4. QDWH in FP64 only on the small reduced leaves (where n is small enough that FP64's low throughput is affordable) -- FP64 QDWH gives a perfect sign, could enable clean recursion at the leaf.

t7: depth-1 spectral split 1024->2x512 shape-7 dense-subset peel (mean-sigma K=704 NS28 cluster halves). Maps the crossover wall: mean-sigma split UNBALANCED (max_side ~801 vs true 513) -> K=704 misses larger side -> nbad 30-34/36, orth 8.7, shape7 249.7ms (2.4x worse than 105ms), geomean 30504. No cheap sigma (trace/n, Ritz-med, LDL-inertia) balances heterogeneous mixed spectra; true count-median 513 is circular. Needs K~820 (no headroom) at cheap sigma.

t8: depth-1 split-1024 Ritz-median sigma (mp=512) K=768. Ritz-median improves balance (eigr 0.0034 CLEARS gate vs t7 mean 0.146) but orth_max=4.29 -> 28/36 fallback (near-sigma duplicate-column select = _SIGN_DC_HALF_REORTH failure) + Ritz mp=512 adds cost -> shape7 382ms, geomean 31473. Even the best cheap median can't both balance the split AND keep membership orthonormal on heterogeneous mixed spectra.

t9: per-half CQR2 reorth on the split-1024 (the _SIGN_DC_HALF_REORTH duplicate fix). Does NOT help: orth 4.29, nbad 28/36, geomean 31509. The fallback is a BALANCE problem (one side's true count exceeds K=768 per-half capacity for heterogeneous matrices), not within-half orthogonality. Conclusively maps the shape-7 depth-1 crossover: blocked by the un-cheaply-balanceable median of heterogeneous mixed spectra.

t10: consolidate (all recursion machinery off). geomean 28583 = parent 28581 (no regression), 39/39 valid, shapes 6/7/11 at parent. Split-on nsys (t8) confirms the crossover: cluster mega_eigh_clust_split_k=58.8ms DID replace the 1024 cuSOLVER for captured matrices BUT the K~768 block is nearly as costly as whole-1024, PLUS sytrd4_cta=22ms fallback on 28/36 -> pays both. The 2.6x headroom assumed K=512; real required K~768 (unbalanced heterogeneous median) evaporates it. Junk-free depth-2 also blocked (fuzzy FP32 sign -> no clean rank to compress). Both recursion routes blocked by the FP32 near-sigma precision wall.

Resumed on the recursion angle (manager's pivot). 10 committed trials total; FINAL/BEST = t10 711e51be geomean 28583 = parent 28581 (no regression, 39/39 valid, shapes 6/7/11 at parent). Built the depth-1 1024->2x512 split (_eigh_split1024 + peel) and probed junk-free depth-2 compression; both plumbed OFF (measured losses). NO speedup landed -- the recursion crossover is now MAPPED PRECISELY and it sits on the WRONG side for these shapes.

SHAPE-7 DEPTH-1 CROSSOVER (the lever) -- measured, does NOT beat cuSOLVER:
- The 2.6x headroom I quoted assumed K=512 (a BALANCED split). But the split of a HETEROGENEOUS mixed batch cannot be cheaply BALANCED: no cheap sigma hits the true count-median. Measured max_side (larger half count) per estimator on shape-7 dense subset: trace/n mean=801, Ritz-median(mp=512)=683, LDL-inertia-bisect=815 (and 16s too slow); TRUE count-median=513 but circular. So K must be ~768-820, giving reduced blocks barely smaller than 1024.
- Live routed cost (t7 K=704 mean-sigma): nbad 30-34/36, orth 8.7, shape7 250ms (2.4x WORSE). (t8 K=768 Ritz-median): eigr CLEARS gate (0.0034) but orth 4.29 -> 28/36 fallback, shape7 382ms. (t9 +per-half CQR2 reorth): no help, orth still 4.29 -- the fallback is a BALANCE problem (one side's true count > K per-half capacity), not within-half orthogonality.
- t8 split-on nsys CONFIRMS the mechanism the manager asked to verify: mega_eigh_clust_split_k=58.8ms DID replace the 1024 cuSOLVER for captured matrices -- BUT the K~768 cluster block is nearly as costly as whole-1024, PLUS sytrd4_cta=22ms fallback on the 28/36 that miss -> pays BOTH. Real routed cost ~= split(21ms NS sign) + cluster(58.8ms at K768) + fallback(22ms) + overhead >> 105ms floor.
- CROSSOVER VERDICT for n=1024: recursion beats cuSOLVER only if K <= ~560 (balanced), which needs a cheap accurate count-median for heterogeneous spectra -- unavailable. At the achievable K~768 the split cost EQUALS/EXCEEDS the saving.

SHAPE-11 DEPTH-2 (junk-free compression, manager's follow-on) -- also blocked:
- Confirmed the reduced +block IS fp32-resolvable and QDWH converges on it (mean||S^2-I||=0.064), so the ONLY blocker is oversample junk, as the manager noted.
- BUT junk-free compression needs to identify the exact-rank + subspace from the fuzzy level-1 sign. Measured: column membership ||P+ u|| of the level-1 basis does NOT cleanly separate at k+ (rank-258 membership 0.43, smooth decay, NO cliff) -- because the FP32 sign is fuzzy (||S^2-I||~3.7 at sigma=0 by the precision wall), so P+ is a fuzzy projector with no sharp rank. Zero-padding to batch-max IS safe at the 2nd split (sigma~0.5, so zero-eigs are far from sigma, sign cleanly), but there's no clean k+ to pad TO.

ROOT CAUSE unifying every negative result: the FP32 near-sigma PRECISION WALL. A clean spectral split/projector needs the eigenvalue nearest sigma resolved; on these spectra that eigenvalue is ~1e-7 relative (=FP32 eps) at the median (shape 11 symmetric-about-0; shape-7 mixed had 9e-11). FP64 resolves it perfectly (QDWH FP64 ||S^2-I||=8e-14) but is too slow on B200. So BOTH recursion routes (depth-1 balance, depth-2 junk-compression) are blocked by the same wall.

STILL OPEN (manager may write briefs):
1. A cheap ACCURATE count-median for heterogeneous spectra would unlock shape-7 depth-1 (the ONLY missing piece; the routing/cluster/gate all work). Candidates not exhausted: a 1-2 step sign-trace Newton correction on sigma (re-center after one cheap sign), or a stochastic-Lanczos-quadrature inertia estimate (cheaper than LDL). If max_side drops to ~560, K=576 cluster ~35ms + sign 21ms + overhead ~15ms ~= 71ms < 105ms.
2. FP64 QDWH ONLY on the small reduced leaves (n<=256 after 2 splits) where FP64's low throughput is affordable and it gives a perfect sign -- could enable a clean deep recursion that FP32 cannot.
3. Shape-7 is heterogeneous; a per-STRUCTURE peel (only the ~36 dense matrices whose median IS estimable) rather than the whole dense-PR window might isolate the balanceable subset.
